# Project Summary / Abstract

This project addresses the *clinical decision gap* between high-performance
predictive models and actionable point-of-care tools for opioid and polypharmacy
risk. Utilizing the Virginia All-Payer Claims Database (APCD)—covering 6.9 million
unique patients—we implement a partition-first architecture achieving a 15.1×
throughput improvement. We apply a novel Consensus-Causal Filter (SHAP ∩ Formal
Feature Attribution; FFA) to identify modifiable drivers of adverse drug events
(ADEs). The project culminates in a privacy-first, serverless PGx Risk Dashboard
providing real-time risk scores and counterfactual "What-If" analysis.

**Project Narrative:** This research moves beyond technically accurate models to
provide user-centric explainability for vulnerable populations. By recovering
pharmacogenomic (PGx) signals from administrative claims, we provide a scalable
framework to reduce preventable mortality associated with polypharmacy and the
opioid epidemic.

{{< pagebreak >}}

# Specific Aims

**Overall Objective:** Apply a standardized CRISP-DM pipeline and the Clinical
OODA Loop (Observe–Orient–Decide–Act) framework to develop and evaluate a
"causal calculator" for opioid and polypharmacy risk prediction from All-Payer
Claims Data.

**Long-Term Goal:** Produce a replicable, causally grounded, and clinically
actionable pipeline from raw claims data to bedside pharmacogenomic decision
support, suitable for adoption by community pharmacies and Safety Net hospitals
without EHR integration.

---

**Aim 1 (RQ1) — Identify Causal Drivers of Opioid-Related Emergency Department
Visits.** Develop an ensemble model (CatBoost/XGBoost) to predict opioid-related
ED visits across seven age bands (13–114) using a strict 2019 prospective holdout.
The Consensus-Causal Filter (SHAP ∩ FFA) will isolate modifiable causal features
from correlated documentation artifacts. Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) clustering
will identify *Rapid-Onset* (4.2-month) and *Chronic-Escalation* (22.1-month)
trajectory archetypes to guide the timing of clinical interventions.

*Expected Outcome:* Ensemble models with AUROC ≥ 0.95 and PR-AUC ≥ 0.84 across
all seven age bands, with DTW archetypes providing intervention windows validated
against 2019 holdout trajectory concordance.

---

**Aim 2 (RQ2) — Develop a "Causal Calculator" for Polypharmacy Interaction
Risk.** Extend FFA to identify synergistic drug-drug interactions (e.g.,
Acetaminophen + Levofloxacin, IE = 16.3) in geriatric populations using FP-Growth
co-occurrence networks and Interaction Effect (IE) scoring. Quantify Intervention
Rate (IR) scores to rank deprescribing priorities based on expected risk reduction
per patient exposure.

*Expected Outcome:* Identification of ≥100 synergistic drug pairs, IR-ranked
deprescribing targets actionable from standard claims data, and a validated Z-code
monitoring analysis distinguishing managed from fragmented-care polypharmacy
phenotypes.

---

**Aim 3 — Translate Causal Rules to Privacy-First Clinical Decision Support.**
Deploy a serverless PGx Risk Dashboard on AWS Lambda bundling up to 84 per-bin
ensemble models. Implement *Imputation of Normality* to maintain risk-band
stability up to 60% input sparsity. Integrate CPIC Level A/B pharmacogenomic
guidance via a stateless, ephemeral gene-drug lookup card satisfying HIPAA
minimum-necessary (45 CFR § 164.502(b)).

*Expected Outcome:* Production-deployed dashboard achieving warm inference ≤ 100 ms,
cold-start ≤ 3,000 ms, 100% CPIC concordance across 573 test cases, and risk-band
stability at ≥ 87% of patients at 50% input sparsity.

# Research Strategy

## Significance

**The Clinical Decision Gap.** Current medication safety tools rely on simple
counts and pairwise drug-drug interaction (DDI) checks, missing the nonlinear
risk escalation of complex polypharmacy regimens. High-performance machine
learning (ML) models for opioid and ADE risk have been published extensively,
yet fewer than 10% of FDA-cleared AI/ML devices include prospective clinical
validation evidence, and fewer still report deployment architecture sufficient
for independent replication [@Rajpurkar2022; @FDA2021].

**The Triple Gap.** Our PRISMA-compliant Systematic Quantitative Literature
Review of 5,839 candidate studies identified three co-occurring gaps in the
existing literature: (1) the near-complete omission of pharmacogenomic (PGx)
context from risk models; (2) the prevalence of temporal leakage—where future
outcome information contaminates training features, producing logically inverted
causal rules (e.g., buprenorphine predicting OUD) [@Kapoor2023]; and (3) the
failure to bridge validated models to deployment. This project directly addresses
all three.

**Population Need.** Virginia's opioid-related ED visit rate has increased by
34% since 2018. Geriatric polypharmacy (≥5 medications) affects 44% of adults
aged 65+ and is the leading modifiable predictor of preventable hospitalizations.
Standard pairwise DDI databases miss synergistic interactions involving three or
more drugs—the very combinations FFA is designed to detect.

## Innovation

This project introduces three conceptual and technical innovations:

**1. The Consensus-Causal Filter (SHAP ∩ FFA).** A feature is designated causal
only when independently confirmed by both distributional (SHAP) and structural
(FFA decision-rule) analysis. This replaces heuristic feature selection with a
two-method gate that demonstrably reduces false-positive causal claims.

**2. Recovery of PGx Signal from Claims.** We demonstrate that CPIC Level A/B
pharmacogenomic features are recoverable from administrative ICD/NDC codes at
population scale, providing a scalable alternative to prospective genotyping for
risk stratification in settings without access to genetic testing.

**3. Privacy-First Serverless CDS.** The "compute, respond, discard" architecture
satisfies HIPAA minimum-necessary without a Business Associate Agreement, enabling
adoption by community pharmacies and Safety Net hospitals for whom institutional
EHR integration is not available.

## Approach

### Data and Architecture

We utilize the Virginia APCD (1.8 TB; 2016–2019), covering 6.9 million unique
patients annually, staged into a Bronze-to-Gold data lake via partitioned DuckDB
workers. The partition-first architecture enforces strict temporal leakage prevention:
a "B1" balancing constraint architecturally prevents any post-outcome features
from appearing in training windows. The 2019 calendar year is held out prospectively
for all model evaluation.

Fifteen Age Band × Cohort partitions (opioid-related ED: 13–64; non-opioid ED:
65–114) are processed in parallel, achieving 15.1× throughput improvement over
single-node processing. The PROBAST checklist was applied to ensure low risk of
bias in predictor selection and analysis.

### Model Selection for Tabular APCD Data

Although I have formal training in deep learning (BIOS 691), this project
deliberately prioritizes tree-based gradient boosting (XGBoost, CatBoost) for
high-dimensional tabular claims data. Comparative studies have shown that XGBoost
outperforms or matches state-of-the-art deep architectures on most tabular
benchmarks while requiring substantially less hyperparameter tuning
[@kadra2021tabular]. A large-scale meta-analysis across 176 tabular datasets
further found that gradient-boosted trees outperform neural networks on average,
particularly on large and statistically irregular datasets with skewed or
heavy-tailed feature distributions—properties characteristic of real-world
claims data [@grinsztajn2023when]. Given the additional requirement for stable,
interpretable SHAP and FFA attributions, tree-based ensembles are the most
appropriate primary modeling choice. Models are tuned via Optuna Bayesian TPE
and validated through Monte Carlo Cross-Validation (MCCV).

### Aim 1 Implementation: Opioid Risk and Trajectory Archetypes

Ensemble risk scores (CatBoost + XGBoost + XGBoost-RF) are computed with
performance-based weighting derived from MCCV PR-AUC and LogLoss on the 2016–2018
training set. The Consensus Filter selects features confirmed by both SHAP
importance and FFA structural attribution. DTW clustering (Sakoe-Chiba band,
*w* = 20%) derives trajectory archetypes from 12-month pre-ED prescription
sequences; archetypes are validated by 2019 holdout concordance and annotated
with clinical intervention windows (30-day PDMP review for Rapid-Onset; physical
therapy and mental health referral windows for Chronic-Escalation).

**Mitigation of risks:** If PR-AUC < 0.80 in low-prevalence bands, cost-sensitive
weighting (class_weight proportional to prevalence) and SMOTE oversampling will
be applied. DTW alignment will fall back to Euclidean distance if Sakoe-Chiba
banding over-constrains short sequences.

### Aim 2 Implementation: FFA Causal Calculator for Polypharmacy

FP-Growth (support ≥ 0.01, confidence ≥ 0.50) generates pre-computed drug
co-occurrence rulesets for the geriatric cohorts (65–74, 75–84, 85–114). FFA
multi-feature interaction testing extends pairwise IE scoring to triplets,
identifying synergistic combinations invisible to standard DDI databases.
Intervention Rate (IR) scores rank deprescribing priorities by expected risk
reduction per patient-exposure. Z-code monitoring status (ICD-10 Z79.x) stratifies
patients by managed vs. unmanaged polypharmacy to identify fragmented-care
phenotypes.

**Mitigation of risks:** If synergistic pair counts fall below 50, support
thresholds will be lowered to 0.005. Z-code analysis is pre-registered as
exploratory if cell counts prohibit propensity-matched comparison.

### Aim 3 Implementation: Production Deployment and Validation

The AWS Lambda container bundles up to 84 per-bin models (3 algorithms × 4
density bins × 7 age bands), CPIC snapshot (573 Level A/B gene-drug pairs), and
per-band density thresholds. Imputation of Normality fills missing features with
training-set medians, maintaining risk-band stability at ≥ 87% of patients at
50% sparsity. The CI/CD pipeline (GitHub Actions → ECR → Lambda) validates each
deployment against automated PR-AUC ≥ 0.60 and LogLoss ≤ 0.50 gates.

**Mitigation of risks:** If Lambda container exceeds 10 GB, model compression
(quantized XGBoost) and cohort-specific container sharding will be applied.
PGx card generation falls back to diplotype-only output if PharmVar lookup fails.

# Research Training Plan

## Overview

The training program is organized around four competency areas aligned with the
Clinical OODA Loop (Observe–Orient–Decide–Act) framework for translational
informatics. All coursework is completed; training activities now focus on
independent research and dissemination.

## Area 1: Advanced Claims-Based Pharmacoepidemiology (Observe)

This area builds foundational skills for managing the Virginia APCD and its 1.8 TB
of longitudinal records.

**Formal Doctoral Coursework:**

- **HGEN 611 – Data Science I** (Fall 2018, B): Computational foundation for
  high-throughput genomic and claims-based data engineering.
- **HGEN 691 – Methods in Data Science** (Spring 2020, A): Advanced feature
  engineering and pipeline design for large-scale biomedical datasets.
- **BIOS 572 – Biomedical Data I** (Fall 2019, B): Statistical methods for
  large-scale biomedical datasets applied to ADE risk assessment.
- **FMBA 614/615/616 – Health Care Management I–III** (Summer 2017, A):
  Regulatory and systems-level context for healthcare delivery and outcomes research.

**Professional Training:** DAPT 611 (Analysis & Design of Database) and
DAPT 614 (Advanced SQL) support the partition-first architecture; DAPT 621/622
(Statistics for Big Data) provide the quantitative foundation for APCD-scale
feature analysis.

## Area 2: Advanced Machine Learning and Causal Discovery (Orient)

This area focuses on moving beyond purely predictive "black-box" models toward
causally interpretable ensembles supporting the Consensus-Causal Filter and
IR scoring.

**Modeling Mastery:**

- **BIOS 691 – Deep Learning with R** (Summer 2020, A): Background in neural
  architectures and regularization. I use this to understand the broader model
  landscape and its limitations on clinical tabular data. Following evidence that
  tree-based gradient boosting (XGBoost, CatBoost) outperforms or matches deep
  learning on heterogeneous tabular datasets—especially large, skewed, and
  irregular datasets typical of health claims—I focus modeling on GBDTs integrated
  with SHAP and FFA rather than neural networks as primary models
  [@kadra2021tabular; @grinsztajn2023when].
- **STAT 591 – Applied Bayesian Statistical Analysis** (Spring 2021, A):
  Theoretical basis for uncertainty quantification; motivates Bayesian TPE
  optimization (Optuna) for tuning tree-based ensembles.
- **DAPT 631 (Data Mining)** and **DAPT 632 (Forecasting Methods)** (Spring/Fall
  2017, A): Applied predictive modeling for longitudinal clinical trajectories,
  informing DTW trajectory archetyping within a tree-based ensemble framework.

**Applied Certification:** AWS Certified Machine Learning – Specialty validates
expertise in designing, deploying, and monitoring large-scale inference pipelines
and stratified ensemble models across age bands and risk strata.

## Area 3: Translational Informatics and Big Data Architecture (Decide & Act)

This area targets deployment of model insights as production-grade clinical
decision support software.

**Applied Certifications:**

- **AWS Certified Big Data Analytics**: Expertise in scaling analytical workloads
  (DuckDB and S3 data lakes) to achieve the 15.1× throughput improvement.
- **AWS Certified Solutions Architect**: Technical basis for deploying the serverless
  PGx Risk Dashboard using the ephemeral AWS Lambda architecture.

**Genomic Foundations:**

- **PHAR 691 – Advanced Pharmacogenomics** (Spring 2020, H): Biological context
  for recovering PGx signals from administrative claims.
- **HGEN 619 – Quantitative Genetics** (Fall 2019, C): Population-level genomic
  variation informing CPIC Level A/B feature engineering.

**Applied Analytics:** DAPT 612 (Text Mining), DAPT 613 (Business Intelligence),
DAPT 615 (Emerging Technologies), DAPT 642 (Risk Analysis) provide the applied
informatics breadth for full-stack clinical AI development.

## Area 4: Geriatrics, Scientific Communication, and Research Ethics (Act)

This area supports transition to independent investigator and communication of
XAI outputs to clinical stakeholders.

- **PHAR 691 – Geriatrics Research Group** (Fall 2023, P): Interdisciplinary
  clinical reviews validating causal calculator findings against geriatric
  prescribing standards (STOPP/Beers criteria).
- **Lean Six Sigma Black Belt** (Villanova): Managing reliability and safety of
  the clinical software lifecycle; reducing process variation in inference pipeline
  deployment.
- **DAPT 642 – Intro to Risk Analysis** (Spring 2017, A): Formal risk assessment
  integrated into the CI/CD pipeline validation gates.
- **FMBA 614–616 – Health Care Management**: Executive-level communication of
  complex XAI outputs to non-technical clinical leadership.

# Candidate's Background and Goals

## Personal Statement

My research goal is to bridge administrative claims data and clinical decision
support using systems theory and military decision theory (OODA loops). As a
Navy veteran and data scientist, I apply rigorous engineering discipline—enforced
by Lean Six Sigma Black Belt training—to translational health informatics problems.
The causal gap between high-performing models and bedside usability is the central
challenge I address in this dissertation.

## Preparedness

**Quantitative foundation:** Graduate training in Bayesian statistics (STAT 591,
A), deep learning (BIOS 691, A), quantitative genetics (HGEN 619), and
pharmacogenomics (PHAR 691) provides the methodological breadth for causal
discovery in multi-omic, claims-based data. Prior M.S. coursework (DAPT series,
all A) established mastery in database architecture, SQL, data mining, and
forecasting—directly applied to the partition-first APCD pipeline.

**Engineering credentials:** AWS certifications (Solutions Architect, Machine
Learning Specialty, Big Data Analytics) validate production-grade deployment
competency. The PGx Risk Dashboard is currently live at sub-100 ms warm inference.

**Demonstrated productivity:** Five dissertation manuscripts are complete or in
submission across four peer-reviewed journals (CTS, CPT:PSP, CPT), documenting
a complete pipeline from APCD-scale data engineering to serverless CDS deployment.

## Potential

The Clinical OODA Loop framework I developed integrates OODA decision theory with
CRISP-DM methodology to create a reproducible, generalizable pipeline for
translational clinical AI. This framework is designed to be replicable by any
research team with access to an all-payer claims database and standard cloud
infrastructure, with no proprietary EHR integration required.

# Compliance and Data Management

## Human Subjects

This project is a claims-based secondary analysis of de-identified records.
**VCU IRB Protocol HM20022300** (non-human-subjects waiver) is in place, granted
by the Virginia Center for Health Innovation (VCHI) Data Use Agreement.
No identifiable patient data are collected, stored, or transmitted at any stage.

## Privacy-by-Design

The PGx Risk Dashboard follows a "compute, respond, discard" pattern:

- Patient-linked inputs are processed in Lambda memory and discarded at function
  termination.
- No PII is written to S3, databases, or logs.
- The CPIC PGx card accepts only SNP variant data (no name, DOB, or identifiers);
  results are streamed directly to the client as a downloadable PDF.
- HIPAA minimum-necessary (45 CFR § 164.502(b)) is satisfied architecturally
  without a Business Associate Agreement.

## Data Management and Sharing

Code, derived network feature specifications, and analysis scripts are shared via
GitHub (github.com/Jerome3590/pgx-analysis) to ensure exact computational
reproducibility. Manuscript submission packages (DOCX + TIFFs + supplementary
tables) are maintained in the same repository. No individual-level claims data
are shared; only aggregate model outputs and feature importance summaries.

## Responsible Conduct of Research

Training focuses on: (1) data privacy and HIPAA compliance in AI healthcare
applications; (2) ethics of algorithmic decision support for vulnerable populations;
(3) reproducibility standards including pre-registered holdout splits and public
code release; and (4) dual-use considerations for prescribing-behavior prediction
systems.
